capacity.value: One-shot at every dilution; a litre of working solution per roll

reuse.value: Never reused. A staining, compensating pyro developer mixed from two concentrates: it gives a long scale, fine grain and a stain that helps alt-process printing. It is mixed by ratio of A + B + water, so the parts fields are left blank deliberately.

Never reused. PMK is the classic pyrogallol staining developer: it tans the emulsion, gives edge sharpness and a stain that is useful for platinum and other alt processes. It is toxic and stains everything it touches, including skin and trays.

capacity.value: 1 US gallon of each bath: dozens of rolls, replenished by topping up and replacing when exhausted

reuse.value: Two baths, reused and topped up. Development is by absorption in Bath A and activation in Bath B, so it is largely time- and temperature-tolerant; the published routine is a fixed time in each bath rather than a single developing time. It is the classic push developer for Tri-X.

capacity.value: 1 US quart stock: about 8–10 rolls with replenishment

reuse.value: Reusable with an Acufine replenisher. A high-acutance speed-increasing developer from the 1950s, still used for pushing and for its crisp, slightly grainy look.

capacity.value: One-shot at 1+10; 1 litre of working solution per roll

reuse.value: Never reused. A fine-grain liquid developer with good keeping qualities, popular in Europe as an alternative to ID-11.

capacity.value: 1 litre stock: about 8 rolls; 1+1 uses 250 ml per roll

reuse.value: Diluted solutions are one-shot. Foma's ascorbate fine-grain developer, a low-toxicity alternative to D-76 with similar fine-grain behaviour.
Never reused. An HC-110 equivalent made in Italy, with the same dilution letters and a similar curve.

Never reused. A developer made from instant coffee, washing soda and vitamin C, documented by the community rather than a manufacturer. Development times vary with the coffee used, so it is a developer to test rather than trust; its results are real, its times are not standardised.
